habit_line: Focus habit: Notice - Pause on the picture or the numbers and let the child say what they see before you name anything. Say: “What do you see? What stays the same, what changes?” Do not give the answer first: ask the prompt, wait, and give a hint only if the child is stuck.

say: Hello, pattern machines! Today we find out what is far, far along a pattern, like the 41st shape, without drawing all 41.
The secret is groups. If we know the group, the times tables tell us where every group ends.
do: Focus habit: Notice - Pause on the picture or the numbers and let the child say what they see before you name anything. Say: “What do you see? What stays the same, what changes?” Do not give the answer first: ask the prompt, wait, and give a hint only if the child is stuck.

say: Clap, clap, stomp. Clap, clap, stomp. Keep it going with me!
Freeze! What will we do on beat 9? On beat 10? How do you know?
Our cube train goes red, red, blue, red, red, blue. What colour do you think cube 20 will be? Write your guess before you build.
stuck: Stuck: put a finger on each blue cube. Say their numbers. What do you notice?
The blue cubes are at 3, 6, 9 … Which table is that? Keep counting in 3s.
Finished early: what colour is cube 30? Cube 31? Explain without building.

say: "Sun, moon, star, sun, moon, star. The group is 3 shapes long. Every group ends with a star, at 3, 6, 9, 12: the 3 times table. Place 14? 12 is the end of a group, so 13 starts again with a sun, and 14 is a moon."
"Where is the 5th star? There is one star at the end of each group, so the 5th star ends the 5th group: 5 × 3 = 15."
"Squares made of sticks: 4, 7, 10. Each new square needs only 3 more sticks because it shares a side. I make a table and keep adding 3."

do: Ask: "How long is one group? Where does each group end?"
Ask: "Is that place the first shape of a group or the last?"
Ask: "What is the rule? Does it work for every pair in your table?"
stuck: Hint 1: "Draw a line after each group. Count the groups."
Hint 2: "Find the nearest times-table number before your place. That shape ends a group."
Hint 3: "Make a table and look at how much it goes up each time."

say: "A pattern repeats every 5 shapes. Is the 10th shape always the same as the 20th?"
ask: "A pattern repeats every 5 shapes. Is the 10th shape always the same as the 20th?"

Yes: 10 and 20 are both in the 5 times table, so both are the last shape of a group. (If it repeated every 3 shapes the answer would be no: 9 ends a group, so 10 is the 1st shape; 18 ends a group, so 20 is the 2nd shape.)

say: "You did not draw 41 shapes today. You found the group, used a times table and counted on. That is how pattern machines think."

p2l4-title.note: Objective: Find far places in a repeating pattern by counting in groups (the ends of the groups are in a times table); count how many of one shape there are; describe a growing pattern with a table and a rule and use it forwards and backwards; find the numbers that two counting patterns share. Tables used: 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 only. Thinking strategies taught today: LOOK FOR A PATTERN (group size, where groups end) and MAKE A TABLE / MAKE A LIST (growing patterns, two counting lists). Materials: Linking cubes in 3 colours (about 20 per pair), mini whiteboards, matchsticks or lolly sticks (about 25 per pair), counters. Online: Coloured pencils and squared paper (or Lego bricks) for the cube train; children draw sticks for the growing pattern and check their tables against the slide. Time plan: opening 0 to 1.5, sneak-peek puzzles 1.5 to 6, warm-up 6 to 10.5, explore 10.5 to 23.5, mini-lesson 23.5 to 35.5, brain break 35.5 to 38.5, worksheet page 1 38.5 to 52.5, check together, page 1 52.5 to 55, short teaching 55 to 57.5, worksheet page 2 57.5 to 69, check together, page 2 69 to 71.5, flex (spare time) 71.5 to 76.5, talk time 76.5 to 81.5, exit ticket 81.5 to 86.5, looking back 86.5 to 88.5, closing and stamps 88.5 to 90. The Think harder and Go further slides are optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Kit ready at minute 0: ask families to put every item on the desk before the lesson starts (a 30-second check at the start). SPINE: Today's tool is Spot the pattern. Look for what repeats or grows. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook. HABIT: Focus habit: Notice. Pause on the picture or the numbers and let the child say what they see before you name anything. Say: "What do you see? What stays the same, what changes?" Do not give the answer first: ask the prompt, wait, and give a hint only if the child is stuck.

p2l4-tool.note: SPINE: Show for about 20 seconds, inside the opening. Today's tool is Spot the pattern. Look for what repeats or grows. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

p2l4-precheck.note: Minutes 1.5 to 6. Sneak-peek puzzles: two puzzles on the key idea of today, which the children have NOT learnt yet. Say out loud (about 28 words): "Two sneak-peek puzzles on ideas we have not learnt yet. Guessing is welcome, so is I do not know. Nobody is marked. Say your answer together on three." Question 1 is an access question: any child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone has a first win (about 45 seconds). Question 2 is the thinking question (about 90 seconds). Then about 2 minutes for the answers slide and the move on. Answers are PRIVATE: each child writes on their own paper and says the answer together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Do not raise whiteboards together, do not read answers out, do not name children. Q1 answer: A square (the squares are the 3rd, 6th and 9th shapes). Listen for: Drawing it out is a fine method. Listen for "every 3rd one is a square". Q2 answer: A moon. Listen for: Groups of 4: 20 is the end of a group (5 groups of 4), so the 21st is a star and the 22nd is a moon. Drawing 22 shapes is also fine. At the end click to show the answers as "one way to think about it", without saying who had what. Ask only for volunteers: "Would anyone like to tell us how they started?" Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Never announce who is on which page. Pairs are not split unless both children agree. Children can move either way at any time. Everyone joins explore, the mini-lesson, the check-together slides and talk time.

p2l4-warm1.note: Minutes 6 to 8.5. Pattern rhythm: about 90 seconds of rhythm, then the three beat questions. Everyone stands. Do clap, clap, stomp together for a few rounds while counting the beats aloud. Freeze, then ask each question; take predictions before clicking. Answers: beat 9 is a stomp (stomps are on 3, 6, 9: the 3 times table); beat 10 is a clap (9 ends a group, so 10 is the first beat of the next group); beat 20 is a clap (18 ends a group, 19 is clap 1, 20 is clap 2). Ask: "Which beats are stomps?" (3, 6, 9, 12 …). "How did you find beat 20 without clapping 20 times?" Online: children clap and stomp in view of the camera. A game of about 2.5 minutes: stop it on the clock even if the game is not finished.

p2l4-warm2.note: Minutes 8.5 to 10.5. Read each one aloud, take answers, then click to show. Answers: 16 and 15. Ask for the rule each time: add 4; add 3. Spare questions in the guide table: 50, 45, 40, __ is 35 (take away 5); the 10th number counting in 4s is 40; 2, 5, 8, 11, __ is 14 (not the 3 times table: each number is 1 less than a 3 times table number). Ask quick questions 1 and 3 only (about 2 minutes): children answer by thumbs, hands, not by naming a child. The other questions are spare.

p2l4-explore1.note: Minutes 10.5 to 19.5. Pairs build 9 cubes, then STOP and write a prediction for cube 20 before building on. Ask: "How could you know without building?" Online: children colour squares on squared paper or use Lego. The answers are in the next slide's notes. Go further (a second what-if, so nobody waits) is the box at the foot of this slide; the question is also posted in the chat when the pairs go to their breakout rooms. It is for ANY child who finishes the explore task or wants more: say it to the whole group as a choice, never as a prize, and never name who tries it. Pairs stay together unless both children agree to split. Answer: Cube 20 is green (the green cubes are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20). Cube 30 is red (28 is green, 29 and 30 are red). Take it at the debrief only if a pair offers it.

p2l4-explore2.note: Minutes 19.5 to 23.5. Gather the pairs and take answers. Answers: 1) Red. 2) The blue cubes are at 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18; then 19 and 20 are red. 3) The blue cubes are the 3 times table, because each group of 3 ends with a blue. Push: "What colour is cube 30? Cube 31?" (blue; red). Say: "The group is 3 cubes long, so the 3 times table tells us where each group ends. Today we use that idea to jump far along a pattern." Keep it moving (about 4 minutes in all): ask "how do you know?" on question 2 only; about 15 seconds of talk on the other questions.

p2l4-teach1.note: Minutes 23.5 to 25.5. Teach. Point to the dashed lines: "Each line marks the end of a group." Click to reveal each step. Think-aloud: "Sun, moon, star, sun, moon, star. The group is 3 shapes long. Every group ends with a star, at 3, 6, 9, 12: the 3 times table. Place 14? 12 is the end of a group, so 13 starts again with a sun, and 14 is a moon." Ask: "Is 12 the first shape of a group or the last?" (the last). Children often say "12 is in the 3 times table so it is a sun"; point at place 3, 6 and 9 to show they are stars.

p2l4-we1.note: Minutes 25.5 to 28. Click to reveal the left steps and answer, then the right. Think-aloud: "Where is the 5th star? There is one star at the end of each group, so the 5th star ends the 5th group: 5 × 3 = 15." "How many moons in the first 21 shapes? 21 is in the 3 times table: 7 groups. One moon in each group, so 7 moons." Ask: "How many suns in the first 22 shapes?" (8: 7 groups, and place 22 starts the 8th group with a sun).

p2l4-teachcount.note: Minutes 28 to 29.5. Teach before worksheet page 1 (Q3 counts beads in groups). Click through. Think-aloud: "Every group has exactly 1 blue bead, so counting blue beads counts the groups. 5 groups. Each group has 3 green: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. Each group has 4 beads: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20." Ask: "Why did it matter that the string ends with green beads?" (So the last group is complete; if it stopped right after a blue bead, the last group would have no green.)

p2l4-teachtimes.note: Minutes 29.5 to 31. Teach (moved into the mini-lesson, ahead of worksheet page 2 Q4, flower petals). Click: the legs row, the rule, going forwards, going backwards. Think-aloud: "Each stool adds 3 legs, so the table is the 3 times table. To go forwards I multiply: 10 × 3 = 30. To go backwards from 24 legs I count in 3s until I reach 24: 3, 6, 9 … 24 is 8 threes, so 8 stools." Ask: "What about 20 legs?" (6 stools use 18, and 2 legs are left over: not enough for another stool.)

p2l4-teachgrow.note: Minutes 31 to 32.5. Teach (moved into the mini-lesson, ahead of worksheet page 2 Q5, tables and chairs). Build the squares with lolly sticks. Ask: "How many more sticks for the next square? Why not 4?" (it shares a side with the square before). Click: the sticks row, the note, the step, the answer. Think-aloud: "I make a table. 4, 7, 10: it goes up by 3 each time. I keep adding 3 to reach 10 squares: 31. To go backwards from 22 sticks, I keep adding 3 until I reach 22 and read the squares: 7." Watch for: 10 × 3 = 30 or 10 × 4 = 40. Point at the first square: it needs 4, not 3.

p2l4-try1.note: Minutes 32.5 to 34.5. Whiteboards, then click. The group is 4 beads: groups end with yellow at 4, 8, 12, 16. a) 12 ends a group: yellow. b) 12 ends a group; 13 red, 14 red, 15 blue. c) Blue is 3rd in each group: 3, 7, 11, so bead 11. Ask: "Which table helped?" (the 4 times table).

p2l4-key.note: Minutes 34.5 to 35.5. Say the key idea together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Saying a times-table place (like 20 for a group of 5) is the FIRST shape of a group, when it is the LAST. (2) Counting the whole pattern one by one instead of jumping to the end of a group. (3) Growing patterns: multiplying by the step and forgetting the start (10 squares: 10 × 3 = 30, forgetting the extra stick).

p2l4-break.note: Minutes 35.5 to 38.5. Three minutes: two of movement, one for a drink of water. Take predictions first. Move 15 is a squat (15 is in the 3 times table, so it ends a group). Online: children move in view of the camera.

p2l4-ws1.note: Minutes 38.5 to 52.5. Walk around. Ask "How long is one group? Where does each group end?" before giving any help. Q2(c) (30 letters, count the Ts) and Q3(b) (beads altogether) are marked ★ take-home on the page: children do them at home. Say once, to everyone: "After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder." Never say who is on which page. Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Pairs are not split unless both children agree.

p2l4-ws1ans.note: Minutes 52.5 to 55. Click each answer after a pair explains. Q1: 20 ends a group (square); 23 is the 3rd shape (circle); 40 ends a group, so 41 is the 1st shape (triangle); (the circles in the first 30 shapes is Think harder 1: 6 groups with 2 circles each). Q2: 16 ends a group, so 18 is the 2nd letter, A; every H ends a group, the 10th at 4 × 10 = 40; Ts are at 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, and 29, 30 are M, A. Q3: 12 red is 6 groups; 6 × 3 = 18 yellow; 6 × 5 = 30 beads. Q2(c) and Q3(b) are take-home stars: the answers stay here so children can mark them at home.

p2l4-teachboth.note: Minutes 55 to 57.5. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q6 uses 3s and 4s). Click: Ali's list, Mei's list, the answer, the note. Children circle the numbers that appear in both lists. Say: "MAKE A LIST: write both counts in order, then look for the numbers in both." Ask: "What would the next one after 30 be?" (40).

p2l4-ws2.note: Minutes 57.5 to 69. Children work alone. Q4(d) (23 petals) and Q5(d) (why does it go up by 2) are marked ★ take-home on the page: children do them at home. Note who needs a short catch-up next lesson. For Q5 ask: "How many more children when you add a table?" (the why is the take-home part). Tutor rule at minute 57.5: if the clock is more than 2 minutes late, drop the last Core question of page 2 to take-home (children draw a star beside it). Never shorten talk time, the exit ticket, looking back or the closing. Questions marked with a star and the words take-home on the page are done at home; their answers are still on the check-together slide.

p2l4-ws2ans.note: Minutes 69 to 71.5. Click each answer after a child explains (answer lines only). Q4(d) and Q5(d) are take-home stars: do not use class time on them. Q4: 23 petals: 4 flowers use 20, 3 petals left over. Q5: the rule is add 2: each new table adds 1 child on top and 1 below, and the 2 end seats stay; 10 tables seat 22; 9 tables seat 20. Q6: Ali 3, 6, 9 … 36 (12 numbers); Mei 4, 8 … 36 (9 numbers); both 12, 24, 36.

p2l4-stretch.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Open to any child who chooses it (the choice after question 3 on the worksheet). These are the SAME four questions as the printed Think harder page: the slide shows 1 to 3 and question 4 is on the page only. Never announce who is working on which page. Answers: 1) 12 circles (30 shapes is 6 groups of 5, with 2 circles in each group). 2) Mei is not right. The pattern repeats every 4 beads and 28 ends a group (4 × 7 = 28), so the 29th bead is red and the 30th bead is red. Green beads are the 4th bead of each group: places 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 and 28. 3) 12 yellow beads (18 beads is 6 groups of 3, with 2 yellow in each). 4) (Question: Houses are made of sticks in a row. 1 house uses 5 sticks, 2 houses use 9 sticks, 3 houses use 13 sticks. How many sticks are needed for 6 houses?) 25 sticks. The rule is add 4: 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25.

p2l4-challenge.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Pairs try first, then use the "see it" slide if stuck, then the walk-through. These are Q6 and Q7 on the Think Harder page. Answers: 1) Tower 10 has 29 cubes. Tower 17 has 50 cubes (3 × 17 − 1). No tower has 100, because every tower is 1 less than a 3 times table number and 101 is not in the 3 times table. 2) 8 and 20.

p2l4-chdiag.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Show after pairs have tried the Go further, or if they are stuck. The pictures show the problem, not the answer. Ask: What do you notice? How many more cubes in each new tower? Where does each frog land after its first jump? Could you make a table or two lists?

p2l4-chwalk.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Use after pairs have tried. Q1: each tower has 3 more cubes than the one before; keep the table going until 29. A strong child may notice each tower is 1 less than the 3 times table (tower 10: 30 − 1 = 29), which answers the extra questions: 50 + 1 = 51 is in the 3 times table (17 × 3), so tower 17 has 50 cubes; 100 + 1 = 101 is not (99 and 102 are), so no tower has 100. Q2: list each frog's landings in order up to 30 and circle the numbers in both lists. The next shared number would be 32 (they meet every 12 steps: 8, 20, 32).

p2l4-skill1.note: Optional slide for pairs who finish early or ask for more. Show it only on request and never announce who is working on it. Children write the answer on their own paper and say it together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Answers and tutor lines are for you only. Item 1 (Sequences: the gap grows by 1 each time; tool of the day idea: Make a table). SAY: "This pattern does not add the same number. Make a table and put the gaps in a row of their own." ASK: "What are the gaps? How does the gap change? What is the next gap?" LISTEN FOR: "The gap goes up by 1." ANSWER: a) 21 and 27 (the gaps are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). b) No: the pattern goes 27, 34, 42 and jumps over 40. Item 2 (Sequences: add the two numbers before; tool of the day idea: Spot the pattern). SAY: "Try the gap row. Does it look like the numbers?" ASK: "What is 2 + 4? What is 4 + 6? What would the next number be?" LISTEN FOR: "Add the two numbers before." Ask them to write the whole list to the 9th number. ANSWER: a) 26 and 42 (6 + 10 = 16, 10 + 16 = 26, 16 + 26 = 42). b) 110: the numbers are 2, 4, 6, 10, 16, 26, 42, 68, 110.

p2l4-talk.note: Minutes 76.5 to 81.5. Pairs talk for 90 seconds, then two volunteers share. Answer: yes, 10 and 20 are both in the 5 times table, so both are the LAST shape of a group. (If a pair finishes early and wants more, not as a second question for the group: what if it repeats every 3 shapes? Then 9 ends a group, so 10 is the 1st shape, and 18 ends a group, so 20 is the 2nd.) Praise the reasons, not only the answers. Talk time rules: you choose volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"); never cold-call a child by name; any child may say pass; no public tallies, scores or rankings.

p2l4-exit.note: Minutes 81.5 to 86.5. Answer: a circle. 15 ends a group (5 groups of 3), so 16 is a triangle and 17 is a circle. Extension: make your own repeating pattern of 4 shapes and write 3 far-place questions about it for a partner, with the answers. Children keep slips on their desks and tick them against the answer on the next click; nothing is held up. About 2 minutes of child work.

p2l4-reflect.note: SPINE: Minutes 86.5 to 88.5. Start the timer (90 seconds). Say: "Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one line, or pass. If you are still stuck, tick the box and I will come." Children tick the Look back box on the Choose and look-back page of their workbook, or just tick on paper. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out; the tutor may look at it afterwards. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the open session next lesson (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby; never a direct message). Do not ask children to share. Praise a check you saw, not speed. Then stamp the journals. After the look-back, minutes 88.5 to 90 are flex time (the buffer): finish stamps, then goodbye. Do not start anything new. HABIT: Focus habit: Notice. Pause on the picture or the numbers and let the child say what they see before you name anything. Say: "What do you see? What stays the same, what changes?" Do not give the answer first: ask the prompt, wait, and give a hint only if the child is stuck.
